origin: The post reports the correlation and the self-reports accurately. It overstates with the headline's "Eats Away" and the first paragraph's "eat away at users’ faith in their own abilities, resulting in lower confidence", which are causal claims drawn from a correlational self-report study that disclaims causal inference. Expected honest rating: 40 to 65 (drafter's range, set with the dropped fourth paragraph included; that paragraph held the strongest causal line, "degrades your capacity for independent reasoning", so the start may sit toward the top of the range).

evidence_down.evidence_note: Real. Retraction Watch, "CEO of AI company loses paper on cognitive impact of generative AI", published 2026-09-14, https://retractionwatch.com/2026/09/14/american-psychological-association-technology-mind-behavior-sarah-baldeo-id-quotient/, reporting the journal's retraction notice dated 2026-08-31 (https://psycnet.apa.org/fulltext/2028-19247-001.html). The journal retracted the paper after its sole author and the approving ethics body, the author's own company ID Quotient Advisory Group, declined to share participant-level data and analytic syntax requested in the journal's investigation. The notice says Middlesex University "formally indicated that the research was not approved, conducted, or supervised by the University, and requested withdrawal of its affiliation from the article." The reasons for the investigation come from Retraction Watch, 2026-06-16 (https://retractionwatch.com/2026/06/16/technology-mind-behavior-apa-journal-investigation-cognitive-impact-generative-ai/): questions about "study design, data analysis and ethics approval"; the critic's word was "mathematically impossible", and only one figure (Fig. 2) had the bar problem.
pushes: New information that adds to the fact sheet: on August 31, 2026, Technology, Mind, and Behavior retracted the study. Researchers had publicly questioned the study's design, data analysis and ethics approval, including results that appeared mathematically impossible and a figure whose bars did not match their labels, and the journal opened an investigation. When the journal requested participant-level data and analysis code, the author and the ethics body that approved the study, which is the author's own company, declined to provide them. Middlesex University told the journal the research was not approved, conducted or supervised by the university and asked for its affiliation to be removed. Does that change your rating?
Makes sense. What is your final number?
